zh: 合同稿子是拟好了，但由于设立茧行需要呈请户部核准，方能开张，宓本常便以此为借口，主张等『部照』发下来，再签合同。胡雪岩与古应春哪里知道他心存叵测？只认为订合同只是一个形式，只要把收买新式缫丝厂这件事说好了，款子随时可以动用，所以都同意了。在上海该办的事都办了，胡雪岩冒着溽暑赶回杭州；原来胡三小姐的红鸾星动，有人做媒，由胡老太太作主，许配了『王善人』的独养儿子。王善人本名王财生，与胡雪岩是多年的朋友，年纪轻的时候，都是杭州人戏称为『柜台猢狲』的商店伙计，所不同的是行业，王财生是一家大酱园的『学徒』出身。当胡雪岩重遇王有龄，青云直上时，王财生仍旧在酱园里当伙计，但到洪杨平定以后，王财生摇身一变，以绅士姿态出现，有人说他之发财是由于『趁火打劫』；有人说他『掘藏』掘到了『长毛』所埋藏的一批金银珠宝。但不管他发财的原因是什么，他受胡雪岩的邀约，同办善后，扶伤救死，抚缉流亡，做了许多好事，博得个『善人』的美名，却是事实。杭州克复的第二年，王财生得了个儿子，都说他是行善的报应。
en: The contracts were drafted. But a cocoon firm could not open without approval from the Ministry of Revenue, and Mi used this as a pretext to suggest waiting for the ministry licence before signing. Hu and Gu had no suspicion of his malicious intentions. To them the contracts were merely a formality: once the mill purchase was agreed, the money would be available whenever required. They therefore consented. With his Shanghai business concluded, Hu hurried back to Hangzhou through the oppressive summer heat. A marriage had been proposed for his third daughter, and his mother had accepted on her behalf: she was to marry the only son of “Wang the Philanthropist.” Wang, whose personal name was Caisheng, had been Hu’s friend for many years. In their youth both had been shop assistants, the men Hangzhou people jokingly called “counter monkeys,” though in different trades. Wang had begun as an apprentice in a large sauce-making establishment. When Hu renewed his acquaintance with Wang Youling and rose rapidly in the world, Wang Caisheng remained an assistant. After the Taiping rebellion was suppressed, however, he reappeared in the guise of a gentleman. Some said he had enriched himself by looting during the disorder; others that he had unearthed gold, silver, and jewels buried by the rebels. Whatever the source of his fortune, one fact was certain: at Hu’s invitation he helped with reconstruction, tending the wounded, saving the dying, and aiding displaced people. These good works earned him the title “Philanthropist.” In the second year after Hangzhou’s recovery, a son was born to him, and people called it a reward for his charity.

zh: 那年是同治四年乙丑，所以王财生的这个独子，小名阿牛，这年十九岁。王财生早就想跟胡雪岩结亲家，而胡雪岩因为阿牛资质遇鲁，真有其笨如牛之概，一直不肯答应，不道这年居然进学成了秀才；因而旧事重提，做媒的人说∶阿牛天性淳厚，胡三小姐嫁了他一定不会吃亏，而况又是独子；定受翁姑的宠爱。至于家世，富虽远不敌胡雪岩，但有『善人』的名声弥补，亦可说是门当户对，所欠缺的只不过阿牛是个白丁；如今中了秀才，俗语说『秀才乃宰相之根苗』，前程远大，实在是头良缘匹配的好亲事。这番说词，言之成理，加以胡老太太认为阿牛是独子，胡三小姐嫁了过去，即无妯娌，就不会受气，因而作主许婚，只写信告诉胡雪岩有这回事，催他快回杭州，因为择定七月初七『传红』。回到杭州，才知道王家迎娶的吉期也定下了，是十一月初五；为的是王善人的老娘，风烛残年，朝不保夕，急于想见孙媳妇进门；倘或去世，要三年之后才能办喜事，耽误得太久了。这番理由，光明正大，胡老太太深以为是，好在嫁妆是早就备好了的，只要再办一批时新的洋货来添妆就是了。
en: That was the yichou year, the fourth of Tongzhi. The boy, nicknamed A’niu, was now nineteen. Wang had long wanted a marriage connection with Hu, but Hu thought A’niu dull—indeed, as stupid as the ox suggested by his name—and had consistently refused. Unexpectedly, the young man had now passed into the county school as a licentiate, and the proposal was renewed. The matchmaker argued that his honest, kindly nature would ensure that Hu’s daughter was never mistreated. As an only son’s wife, she would also be cherished by her parents-in-law. Wang’s wealth fell far short of Hu’s, but his reputation for benevolence made up the difference; the families could be considered suitable equals. The sole deficiency had been A’niu’s lack of a degree. Now a licentiate, he had a promising future: as the saying went, “A licentiate is the seedling of a chief minister.” It was an excellent match. The argument was reasonable. Hu’s mother particularly valued the fact that, with no brothers-in-law’s wives in the household, her granddaughter would suffer no friction from sisters-in-law. She therefore accepted, merely writing to inform Hu and urge him home: the formal betrothal ceremony was set for the seventh day of the seventh month. On returning, he learned that the wedding too had been fixed, for the fifth day of the eleventh month. Wang’s aged mother was frail and might die at any time; she longed to see her grandson’s bride enter the household. If she died first, the wedding would have to wait three years, an excessive delay. The reasoning was entirely proper, and Hu’s mother agreed. Fortunately the dowry had long been prepared. Only some fashionable foreign goods remained to be added.

zh: 但办喜事的规模，却要等胡雪岩来商量；这件事要四个人来决定，便是胡雪岩与他的母、妻、妾——螺蛳太太。而这四个人都有一正一反的两种想法，除了胡雪岩以外，其余三人都觉得场面应该收束，但胡老太太最喜欢这个小孙女儿，怕委屈了她；胡太太则认为应该一视同仁，她的两个姐姐是啥场面，她也应该一样地风光；螺蛳太太则是为自己的女儿设想，因为开了一个例子在那里，将来自己的女儿出阁，排场也就阔不起来了。至于胡雪岩当然愈阔愈好，但市面不景气，怕惹了批评。因此谈了两天没有结果；最后是胡雪岩自己下了个结论∶『场面总也要过得去，是大是小，相差也有限；好在还有四个月的工夫，到时候再看吧。』『场面是摆给人家看的。』螺蛳太太接口说道∶『嫁妆是自己实惠。三小姐的陪嫁，一定要风光；这样子，到时候场面就小一点，对外说起来是市面不好；对内，三小姐也不会觉得委屈，就是男家也不会有话说。』这番见解，真是面面俱到，胡老太太与胡太太听了都很舒服；胡雪岩则认为惟有如此，就算排场不大，但嫁妆风光，也就不失面子了。
en: The scale of the celebration, however, awaited Hu’s return. Four people had to decide: Hu, his mother, his wife, and his concubine, Madam Luosi. All four had conflicting inclinations. The three women favoured restraint, yet Hu’s mother loved this youngest granddaughter best and feared slighting her. His wife wanted equal treatment: the girl should enjoy the same splendour as her two elder sisters. Madam Luosi thought of her own daughter. A restrained wedding now would set a precedent limiting the display when her daughter married. Hu naturally preferred the grandest possible occasion, but feared criticism in a depressed market. Two days of discussion produced no decision. At last he concluded, “The occasion must be respectable. The difference between a large and small celebration is limited anyway. There are still four months; we shall see how matters stand.” “The celebration is for other people to look at,” Madam Luosi observed. “The dowry brings real benefit. Give Third Miss a splendid dowry, and a smaller celebration will do. Publicly, we can explain that business is poor; privately, she will not feel slighted. Even the bridegroom’s family can have no objection.” This considered every side. Both Hu’s mother and his wife were pleased, while Hu felt that a magnificent dowry would preserve his dignity even without a lavish ceremony.

zh: 『罗四姐的话不错。嫁妆上不能委屈她。不过添妆也只有就现成的备办了。』『那只有到上海去。』胡太太接着她婆婆的话说，同时看着罗四姐。罗四姐很想自告奋勇，但一转念间，决定保持沉默；因为胡家人多嘴杂，即使尽力，必定也还有人在背后说闲话，甚至造谣言∶三小姐不是她生的，她哪里舍得花钱替三小姐添妆。胡雪岩原以为她会接口，看她不作声，便只好作决定了，『上海是你熟，你去一趟。』他说∶『顺便也看看七姑奶奶。』『为三小姐的喜事，我到上海去一趟，是千应万该的。不过，首饰这样东西，贵不一定好；我去当然挑贵的买，只怕买了来，花样款式不中三小姐的意。我看，』螺蛳太太笑一笑说∶『我陪小姐到上海，请她自己到洋行、银楼里去挑。』『不作兴的！』胡老太太用一口道地的杭州话说∶『没有出门的姑娘儿，自己去挑嫁妆，传出去把人家笑都笑煞了。』『就是你去吧！』胡雪岩重复一句。
en: “Sister Luo is right. We must not stint the dowry. But the additions will have to be bought ready-made.” “Then someone must go to Shanghai,” Hu’s wife said after her mother-in-law, looking at Madam Luosi. Madam Luosi wanted to volunteer, but reconsidered and remained silent. There were too many tongues in the household. However hard she tried, someone would talk behind her back, perhaps alleging that she begrudged the expense because Third Miss was not her own daughter. Hu had expected her to respond. When she did not, he decided for her. “You know Shanghai. Go there, and visit the Seventh Lady while you are about it.” “Of course I should go for Third Miss’s wedding. But expensive jewellery is not necessarily pleasing. Naturally I would choose costly pieces, yet their designs might not suit her taste.” She smiled. “Why not let me take her and have her choose for herself at the foreign firms and jewellers?” “Quite improper!” the Old Madam exclaimed in broad Hangzhou speech. “An unmarried girl choosing her own dowry! People would laugh themselves sick if they heard of it.” “You go yourself,” Hu repeated.

zh: 螺蛳太太仍旧不作承诺，『不晓得三小姐有没有兴致去走一趟？』她自语似地说。『不必了。』胡太太∶『三丫头喜欢怎么样的首饰，莫非你还不清楚？』最后还是由胡老太太一言而决，由螺师太太一个人到上海去采办。当然，她要先问一问胡三小姐的爱好，还有胡太太的意见，同时最要紧的是，一个花费的总数，这是只有胡雪岩才能决定的。『她这副嫁妆，已经用了十几万银子了。现在添妆，最多再用五万银子。』胡雪岩说∶『上海银根很紧，银根紧，东西一定便宜，五万银子起码好当七万用。』
en: Madam Luosi still would not commit herself. “I wonder whether Third Miss might enjoy a visit,” she murmured, as if to herself. “There is no need,” Hu’s wife said. “Surely you know what jewellery she likes.” Finally the Old Madam settled the matter: Madam Luosi would go alone. She would, of course, first consult the girl’s preferences and Hu’s wife’s wishes. Most important was a spending limit, which only Hu could set. “The dowry has already cost over a hundred thousand taels. Spend no more than another fifty thousand on additions. Money is tight in Shanghai, so goods must be cheap. Fifty thousand should buy at least seventy thousand’s worth.”

zh: 到了上海，由古应春陪着，到德商别发洋行里一问，才知道胡雪岩的话适得其反。国内的出产，为了脱货求现，削价出售，固然不错，但舶来品却反而涨价了。『古先生，』洋行的管事解释∶『局势一天比一天紧，法国的宰相换过了，现在的这个叫茹斐理，手段很强硬，如果中国在越南那方面，不肯让步，他决心跟中国开仗。自从外国报纸登了法国水师提督孤拔到越南的消息以后，各洋行的货色，马上都上涨了一成到一成五；现在是有的东西连出价都买不到了。』『这是为啥？』螺蛳太太发问。『胡太太，战事一起，法国兵舰封住中国的海口，外国商船不能来；货色断档，那时候的价钱，老实说一句，要多少就是多少，只问有没有，不问贵不贵，所以现在卖一样少一样，大家拿好东西都收起来了。』『怪不得！』螺蛳太太指着玻璃柜子中的首饰说∶『这里的东西，没有一样是看得上眼的。』『胡太太的眼光当然不同。』那管事说道，『我们对老主顾，不敢得罪的。胡太太想置办哪些东西，我开保险箱，请胡太太挑。』螺蛳太太知道，在中国的洋人，不分国籍，都是很团结的；他们亦有『同行公议』的规矩，这家如此，另一家亦复如此，『货比三家不吃亏』这句话用不上，倒不如自己用『大主顾』的身分来跟他谈谈条件。
en: In Shanghai, Gu accompanied her to the German firm Biefa. Their first inquiries showed that the opposite was true. Domestic products were indeed being discounted for ready cash, but imported goods had risen in price. “The situation grows more tense every day, Mr Gu,” the manager explained. “France has a new premier, Jules Ferry, a very determined man. If China refuses to yield over Vietnam, he means to go to war. Ever since the foreign newspapers reported Admiral Courbet’s arrival in Vietnam, goods at every foreign firm have risen by ten to fifteen per cent. Some things cannot now be bought at any price.” “Why?” Madam Luosi asked. “If war begins, French warships will close China’s ports and foreign merchant ships will be unable to enter. Once supplies stop, sellers can ask whatever they please. The question will be whether an article is available, not whether it is dear. Every item sold now is one less for later, so everyone is putting the best goods aside.” “No wonder!” She pointed at the jewellery in the glass cabinets. “There is nothing here I like.” “Your taste is naturally exceptional, Madam Hu. We would not risk offending an old customer. Tell me what you require, and I shall open the safe for you.” Madam Luosi knew that foreigners in China, whatever their nationality, acted together. They too had agreements among traders. One firm would be much like another, so the maxim about comparing three shops would be little use. Better to negotiate as a major customer.

zh: 『我老实跟你说，我是替我们家三小姐来办嫁妆，谈得拢，几万银子的生意，我都作成了你。不然，说老实话，上海滩上的大洋行，不是你别发一家。』听说是几万银子的大生意，那管事不敢怠慢，『办三小姐的嫁妆，马虎不得。胡太太，你请里面坐！』他说∶『如果胡太太开了单子，先交给我，我照单配齐了，送进来请你看。』螺蛳太太是开好了一张单子的，但不肯泄漏底细，只说∶『我没有单子。只要东西好，价钱克己，我就多买点。你先拿两副钻镯我看看。』中外服饰时尚不同，对中国主顾来说，最珍贵的首饰，就是钻镯；那管事一听此话，心知嫁妆的话不假，这笔生意做下来，确有好几万银子，是难得一笔大生意，便愈发巴结了。将螺蛳太太与古应春请到他们大班专用的小客厅，还特为找了个会说中国话的外籍女店员招待；名叫艾敦，螺蛳太太便叫她『艾小姐。』
en: “To be frank, I am buying a dowry for our third daughter. If we agree, I shall give you the entire order—several tens of thousands of taels. Otherwise, Biefa is hardly Shanghai’s only large foreign firm.” The prospect demanded attention. “Third Miss’s dowry must be treated seriously. Please come inside. If you have a list, let me take it and assemble the goods for you to examine.” She had prepared a list but would not reveal her hand. “No list. If the goods are good and the prices reasonable, I shall buy more. First show me two pairs of diamond bracelets.” Chinese and Western fashions differed. To Chinese customers, diamond bracelets were the most precious jewellery. The request confirmed that she really was buying a dowry and that the order might indeed run to tens of thousands. The manager became still more attentive. He escorted her and Gu to the foreign director’s private sitting room and specially brought in a foreign saleswoman who spoke Chinese. Her name was Aidun; Madam Luosi called her “Miss Ai.”

zh: 『艾小姐，你是哪里人？』『我出生在爱丁堡。』艾敦一面调着奶茶，一面答说。螺蛳太太不知道这个地名，古应春便即解释∶『她是英国人。』『喔！』螺蛳太太说道∶『你们英国同我们中国一样的，都是老太后当权。』艾敦虽会说中国话，也不过是日常用语，什么『老太后当权』，就跟螺蛳太太听到『爱丁堡』这个地名一样，瞠目不知所对。这就少不得又要靠古应春来疏通了∶『她是指你们英国的维多利亚女皇，跟我们中国的慈禧太后。』『喔，』艾敦颇为惊异，因为她也接待过许多中国的女顾客，除了北里娇娃以外，间或也有贵妇与淑女，但从没有一个人在谈话时会提到英国女皇。因为如此，便大起好感，招待螺蛳太太用午茶，非常殷勤。接着，管事的捧来了三个长方盒子，一律黑色真皮，上烫金字，打开第一个盒子，蓝色鹅绒上，嵌着一双光芒四射的白金钻镯，镶嵌得非常精致。
en: “Where are you from, Miss Ai?” “I was born in Edinburgh,” she replied while preparing tea with milk. Madam Luosi did not know the place, so Gu explained that she was British. “Then your country is like ours,” Madam Luosi said. “Both are ruled by an old empress dowager.” Aidun’s Chinese covered everyday conversation only. Talk of an “empress dowager ruling” left her as bewildered as the name Edinburgh had left Madam Luosi. Gu had to explain again. “She means your Queen Victoria and our Empress Dowager Cixi.” Aidun was surprised. She had served many Chinese women—courtesans, and occasionally ladies of rank or respectable young women—but none had mentioned the British queen. She warmed to Madam Luosi and served her afternoon tea with particular care. The manager then brought three oblong boxes, all of black leather with gold lettering. Inside the first, a pair of brilliantly sparkling platinum bracelets set with diamonds rested on blue velvet. The workmanship was exquisite.

zh: 仔细看去，盒子虽新，白金的颜色却似有异，『这是旧的？』她问。『是的。这是拿破仑皇后心爱的首饰。』『我不管什么皇后。』螺蛳太太说∶『嫁妆总是新的好。』『这两副都是新的。』另外西副，一副全钻，一副镶了红蓝宝石，论贵重是全钻的那副，每一只有四粒黄豆大的钻石，用碎钻连接，拿在手里不动都会闪耀；但谈到华丽，却要算镶宝石的那副。『什么价钱？』『这副三万五，镶宝石的这副三万二。』管事的说∶『胡太太，我劝你买全钻的这副，虽然贵三千银子，其实比镶宝的划算。』螺蛳太太委决不下，便即说道∶『艾小姐，请你戴起来我看看。』
en: On closer inspection, however, the box looked new while the metal’s colour seemed otherwise. “These are used?” she asked. “Yes. They were favourite jewels of Napoleon’s empress.” “I care nothing for empresses. New things are better for a dowry.” “Both these other pairs are new.” One was set entirely with diamonds; the other combined diamonds with rubies and sapphires. The all-diamond pair was the more valuable. Each bracelet held four diamonds the size of soybeans, linked by smaller stones, and glittered even when held still. For splendour, however, the coloured stones excelled. “What are the prices?” “Thirty-five thousand for these; thirty-two thousand for the pair with coloured stones. I advise the all-diamond pair, Madam Hu. It costs three thousand more but is better value.” Unable to decide, she asked Aidun to put them on.

zh: 艾敦便一只手腕戴一样，平伸出来让她仔细鉴赏，螺蛳太太看了半天转眼问道∶『七姐夫，你看呢？』『好，当然是全钻的这副好，可惜太素净了。』这看法跟螺蛳太太的完全一样，顿时作了决定，『又是新娘子，又是老太太在，不宜太素净。』她向管事说道∶『我东西是挑定了，现在要谈价钱，价钱谈不拢，挑也是白挑。我倒请问你，这副镯子是啥时候来的？』『一年多了。』『那末一年以前，你的标价是多少？』『三万。』『这不相信，你现在只涨了两千银子，一成都不到。』『我说的是实话。』管事的从天鹅绒衬底的夹层中，抽出来一张标鉴说∶『古先生，请你看。』标签上确是阿拉伯字的『三万』；螺蛳太太也识洋数码，她的心思很快，随即说道∶『你刚才自己说过，买全钻的这副划算，可见得买这副不划算。必是当初就乱标的一个码子，大概自己都觉得良心上过不去，所以只涨了一成不到，是不是？』『胡太太真厉害。』管事的苦笑道∶『驳得我都没有话好说了。』
en: Aidun wore one kind on each wrist and held out her arms for inspection. After a long look, Madam Luosi turned to Gu. “What do you think, Brother-in-law?” “The all-diamond pair is better, certainly, but rather too plain in colour.” This exactly matched her own view, and she decided at once. “For a bride, with the Old Madam present, the effect should not be too subdued.” She turned to the manager. “I have chosen. Now we must discuss the price, or choosing is pointless. When did these bracelets arrive?” “More than a year ago.” “What price did you mark them at then?” “Thirty thousand.” “I do not believe it. You have added only two thousand—less than ten per cent.” “It is true.” He drew a label from beneath the velvet lining. “Mr Gu, please look.” The Arabic numerals did indeed read thirty thousand. Madam Luosi could read them too and responded quickly. “You yourself said the all-diamond pair was better value, so this one must be poor value. You must have marked an excessive price originally and felt too guilty to raise it by even ten per cent. Is that not so?” The manager smiled ruefully. “You are formidable, Madam Hu. I have no answer.”

zh: 螺蛳太太一笑说∶『大家驳来驳去，尽管是讲道理，到底也伤和气。这样，镯子我一定买你的，现在我们先看别的东西，镯子的价钱留到最后再谈，好不好？』是，是。『。于是看水晶盘碗、看香水、看各种奇巧摆设；管事的为了想把那副镶宝钻镯卖个好价钱，在这些货色上的开价都格外公道。挑停当了，最后再谈镯价。『这里一共是一万二。』螺蛳太太说道∶『我们老爷交代，添妆不能超过四万银子；你看怎么样？』她紧接着又说∶『不要讨价还价，成不成一句话。』『胡太太，』管事的答说∶『你这一记「翻天印」下来，教我怎么招架？』『做生意不能勉强。镯子价钱谈不拢，我只好另外去物色；这一万二是谈好了的，我先打票子给你。』管事的楞住了，只好示意艾敦招待螺蛳太太喝茶吃点心，将古应春悄悄拉到一边，苦笑着说∶『这胡太太手段我真服了。为了迁就，后来看的那些东西，都是照本卖的，其中一盏水晶大吊灯，盛道台出过三千银子，我们没有卖，卖给胡太太只算两千五。如果胡太太不买镯子，我这笔生意做下来，饭碗都要敲破了。』『她并不是不买，是你不卖。』
en: She smiled. “However reasonable our arguments, too much disputing spoils goodwill. Let us do this: I shall certainly buy the bracelets from you. Show me the other goods first, and we shall settle their price last.” He agreed. They examined crystal plates and bowls, perfumes, and all manner of ingenious ornaments. Hoping to obtain a good price for the gem-set bracelets, the manager priced these other articles especially fairly. Once her choices were complete, they returned to the bracelets. “These goods total twelve thousand,” she said. “My husband told me not to spend more than forty thousand on additions to the dowry. What do you say? No bargaining now—yes or no.” “Madam Hu, how can I withstand such a crushing stroke?” “Business cannot be forced. If we cannot agree on the bracelets, I must look elsewhere. The twelve thousand is settled; I shall draw you a draft for that now.” Stunned, the manager signalled Aidun to serve more tea and refreshments, then quietly drew Gu aside. “I truly admire her methods,” he said with a bitter smile. “To accommodate her, I offered those later goods at cost. Intendant Sheng offered three thousand for one of the large crystal chandeliers, and we refused; I have charged her only two thousand five hundred. If she does not buy the bracelets, this transaction will cost me my job.” “She is willing to buy. You are unwilling to sell.”

zh: 『哪里是我不卖？价钱不对。』古应春说∶『做这笔生意，赚钱其次；不赚也就是赚了！这话怎么说呢？胡财神嫁女儿，漂亮的嫁妆是别发洋行承办的，你想想看，这句话值多少钱？』『原就是贪图这个名声，才各外迁就，不过总价四万银子，这笔生意实在做不下来！』『要亏本？』『亏本虽不至于，不过以后的行情——』『以后是以后，现在是现在。』古应春抢着说道∶『说老实话，市面很坏，有钱的人都在逃难了；以后你们也未见得有这种大生意上门。』管事的沉默了好一会才说了句∶『这笔生意我如果答应下来，我的花红就都要赔进去了。』古应春知道洋行中的规矩，薪金颇为微薄，全靠售货的奖金，看他的神情不象说假话，足见螺蛳太太杀得太凶；也就是间接证明，确是买到了便宜货，因此觉得应该略作让步，免得错过了机会。
en: “It is not that I am unwilling. The price is wrong.” “Profit is secondary here. Even without it, you gain. Consider the value of people saying that Biefa supplied the splendid dowry when Hu, the God of Wealth, married off his daughter.” “That reputation is precisely why I have been so accommodating. But I really cannot conclude the business at forty thousand.” “Would you lose money?” “Not exactly. But future prices—” “The future is the future; this is now. Frankly, trade is poor, and wealthy people are already fleeing the danger. You may not see another order like this later.” After a long silence, the manager said, “If I accept, I shall sacrifice my entire bonus.” Gu knew how foreign firms worked: salaries were modest, and employees depended on sales bonuses. The man seemed truthful. Madam Luosi had plainly bargained very hard—which also confirmed that she was obtaining excellent value. Some concession was needed lest they lose the opportunity.

zh: 『你说这话，我要帮你的忙。』他将声音放极轻，『我作主，请胡太太私下津贴你五百两银子，弥补你的损失。』管事的未餍所欲，但人家话已说在前面，是帮他的忙，倘或拒绝，变成不识抬举，不但生意做不成，而且得罪了大主顾，真正不是『生意经』了。这样一转念头，别无选择，『多谢古先生。』他说∶『正好大班在这里，我跟他去说明白。古先生即然能替胡太太作主，那么，答应我的话，此刻就先不必告诉胡太太。』古应春明白，他是怕螺蛳太太一不小心，露出口风来，照洋人的看法，这种私下收受顾客津贴的行为，等于舞弊，一旦发觉，不但敲破碗饭，而且有吃官司的可能。因而重重点头，表示充分领会。于是，管事的向螺蛳太太告个罪，入内去见大班。不多片刻，带了一名洋人出来，碧眼方颐，留两撇往上翅的菱角须，古应春一看便知是德国人。
en: “In that case, I shall help you,” Gu said, lowering his voice. “I shall take responsibility for having Madam Hu give you five hundred taels privately to compensate for your loss.” The manager wanted more. But Gu had presented this as a favour; refusing would look ungrateful, lose the sale, and offend a major customer. That was hardly sound business. He had no real choice. “Thank you, Mr Gu. The director happens to be here. I shall explain the position to him. Since you can decide for Madam Hu, there is no need to tell her of your promise just yet.” Gu understood. The manager feared that she might carelessly let something slip. To the foreign owners, accepting a private payment from a customer amounted to dishonesty. Discovery could mean not only dismissal but prosecution. Gu nodded emphatically to show that he fully understood. The manager excused himself to Madam Luosi and went to see the director. Soon he returned with a blue-eyed foreigner, square-jawed and wearing an upward-curving moustache. Gu recognized him at once as German.
